name: Great Discoveries
description: Questions covering: Astronomy, Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Biology, Geography, Archaeology...

questions.question: Who is credited with discovering Uranus?
questions.explanation_correct: William Herschel observed Uranus in 1781. He initially thought the moving object was a comet; its planetary orbit was established later.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Flamsteed had previously recorded Uranus as a star; Herschel is credited with recognizing it as a new object. Galle and Halley are associated with other astronomical work.

questions.question: Which astronomer observed Neptune in Berlin in 1846 using a predicted position sent by Urbain Le Verrier?
questions.explanation_correct: Johann Galle observed Neptune near the location calculated by Le Verrier; Heinrich d’Arrest assisted in the search.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Le Verrier made a mathematical prediction, while the question asks for the Berlin observer. Herschel discovered Uranus and Tombaugh discovered Pluto.

questions.question: Who is credited with the discovery of radioactivity?
questions.explanation_correct: Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896 while studying uranium salts. This finding opened the field of nuclear physics.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other scientists made major contributions to related areas of physics and chemistry, but not this initial discovery. Their work came later or addressed different phenomena.

questions.question: Who is credited with discovering penicillin?
questions.explanation_correct: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 after noticing mold inhibited bacterial growth. This led to the development of antibiotics.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are famous for foundational microbiology and antiseptic work, but not penicillin. Their discoveries belong to related scientific advances.

questions.question: Who published a detailed account of blood circulating through the body and returning to the heart in 1628?
questions.explanation_correct: William Harvey presented a systemic circulation model supported by anatomical and quantitative reasoning.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Vesalius and Malpighi made important anatomical contributions. Earlier scholars, including Ibn al-Nafis, had described aspects of pulmonary circulation.

questions.question: Who wrote On the Origin of Species, published in 1859, explaining evolution by natural selection?
questions.explanation_correct: Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species in 1859. Alfred Russel Wallace independently developed natural selection, and their work was jointly presented in 1858.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Wallace independently developed natural selection but did not write Darwin’s 1859 book. Mendel and Lamarck made other contributions to biology.

questions.question: Who is credited with reaching the Americas in 1492?
questions.explanation_correct: Columbus reached islands in the Caribbean in 1492. Indigenous peoples had lived in the Americas for millennia, and Norse seafarers reached North America earlier.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other navigators are associated with different expeditions; none led Columbus’s 1492 voyage.

questions.question: Who is credited with discovering Tutankhamun's tomb?
questions.explanation_correct: Howard Carter discovered Tutankhamun's tomb in 1922 in the Valley of the Kings. The find became one of the most famous in archaeology.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other archaeologists are known for major excavations at different sites. None is credited with this Egyptian tomb discovery.

questions.question: Which fossil collector excavated much of an ichthyosaur skeleton after her brother Joseph found its skull near Lyme Regis?
questions.explanation_correct: Mary Anning excavated the skeleton after Joseph found the skull. The specimen became one of the first scientifically studied ichthyosaurs.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Buckland, Mantell and Owen were important scientists, but the excavation described was carried out by Mary Anning.

questions.question: Who is associated with the discovery of X-rays?
questions.explanation_correct: Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays in 1895 while experimenting with cathode rays. His discovery revolutionized medical imaging and physics.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other scientists made major contributions to electromagnetism, crystallography, or atomic physics, but not X-rays. Their achievements are in related areas, not this discovery.

questions.question: Which scientist proposed a model of the DNA double helix together with Francis Crick in 1953?
questions.explanation_correct: James Watson is one of the scientists most directly associated with proposing the DNA double helix structure. He worked with Francis Crick on the model.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Franklin contributed crucial X-ray diffraction evidence; Pauling and Sanger did not propose the 1953 Watson–Crick model.

questions.question: Which Portuguese explorer reached India by sea around southern Africa in 1498?
questions.explanation_correct: Vasco da Gama’s expedition sailed around the Cape of Good Hope and reached Calicut in 1498, opening a direct sea route from Europe to India.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bartolomeu Dias had rounded southern Africa earlier; the other explorers are associated with different voyages. Indian Ocean maritime trade already existed.

questions.question: Which scientist is known for discovering the tuberculosis bacillus?
questions.explanation_correct: Robert Koch identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis as the bacterium that causes tuberculosis. This was a major breakthrough in microbiology.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are important scientists, but they are associated with different discoveries or fields.

questions.question: Which paleoanthropologist found the 1959 OH 5 skull, originally called Zinjanthropus, at Olduvai Gorge?
questions.explanation_correct: Mary Leakey discovered the OH 5 cranium in 1959. It is now generally classified as Paranthropus boisei.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Louis and Richard Leakey also contributed to paleoanthropology; Donald Johanson is associated with Lucy. Mary found OH 5.

questions.question: Which scientist worked with Pierre Curie on the 1898 discovery of polonium in pitchblende?
questions.explanation_correct: Marie and Pierre Curie identified polonium in pitchblende in 1898. Becquerel had discovered radioactivity in 1896.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Becquerel discovered radioactivity; Rutherford and Planck made different contributions to physics.

questions.question: Which astronomer is credited with discovering Jupiter's four largest moons?
questions.explanation_correct: Galileo discovered Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto in 1610. These are Jupiter's four largest moons.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other astronomers made major contributions to astronomy, but they did not make this discovery.

questions.question: In 1928, Alexander Fleming discovered an antibiotic produced by a genus of fungi with what name?
questions.explanation_correct: Alexander Fleming observed that Penicillium notatum mold inhibited the growth of bacteria.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Streptomyces is used for searching other antibiotics, but not the first one discovered by Fleming.

questions.question: Which scientist used pea-plant crosses to study patterns of inheritance?
questions.explanation_correct: Gregor Mendel’s pea-plant experiments revealed regular patterns of inheritance; inherited traits were known before his work.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Morgan and Bateson were influential geneticists, and Darwin studied evolution, but Mendel conducted the classic pea-cross experiments.

questions.question: Which explorer was the first to reach the South Pole?
questions.explanation_correct: Roald Amundsen reached the South Pole first in 1911. His expedition beat Robert Falcon Scott's party to the pole.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other explorers were famous polar travelers, but they did not achieve the first South Pole arrival.

questions.question: Which archaeologist is best known for excavating Troy?
questions.explanation_correct: Heinrich Schliemann is famously associated with excavations at the ancient site of Troy. His work helped bring the site into wider historical and archaeological attention.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are major archaeologists, but they are associated with different sites or discoveries. They did not excavate Troy.

questions.question: What is the scientific name of the bacterium that Robert Koch proved was the causative agent of 'The White Plague'?
questions.explanation_correct: Robert Koch announced his discovery of this bacterium in 1882, proving it caused tuberculosis.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Vibrio cholerae causes cholera, while E. coli is a common gut bacterium.

questions.question: Which body in the solar system was discovered by Clyde Tombaugh in 1930?
questions.explanation_correct: Pluto was discovered by Clyde Tombaugh at Lowell Observatory in 1930. It remained classified as a planet for decades before being reclassified as a dwarf planet.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are solar-system bodies, but they were discovered by different astronomers or in different eras. They are not the object Tombaugh found.

questions.question: Which researcher conducted the early 1921 pancreatic-extract experiments with Charles Best at the University of Toronto?
questions.explanation_correct: Frederick Banting and Charles Best worked together on early experiments; John Macleod directed the laboratory, and James Collip later contributed purification work.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Macleod was a key contributor and shared the 1923 Nobel Prize with Banting, but the question concerns Banting’s initial experimental partnership with Best.

questions.question: Which hominin species was identified from fossils found at Taung?
questions.explanation_correct: Australopithecus africanus is the species identified from the Taung Child fossil. The Taung discovery was an important early find in human evolution studies.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are hominin species, but they come from different fossil sites or time periods. They are not the species first associated with Taung.

questions.question: Which subatomic particle was identified by J. J. Thomson?
questions.explanation_correct: J. J. Thomson is credited with discovering the electron through cathode-ray experiments. His work showed that atoms contain smaller negatively charged particles.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other particles are important in physics, but they were discovered later or by other researchers. They are not Thomson's discovery.

questions.question: Which explorer is linked with the first sea passage through the Northwest Passage?
questions.explanation_correct: Roald Amundsen is associated with the first successful navigation of the Northwest Passage by sea. His expedition completed the route in the early 20th century.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other explorers are famous polar figures, but they are tied to different expeditions or achievements. They did not complete that sea passage.

questions.question: Which site includes the palace excavated by Arthur Evans?
questions.explanation_correct: Knossos is the Minoan site on Crete where Arthur Evans excavated the palace complex. His work uncovered one of the most famous archaeological sites in the Aegean.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are important ancient sites, but they are distinct from the one Evans excavated. They do not refer to the palace at Knossos.

questions.question: Which gas did Joseph Priestley produce in 1774 by heating mercuric oxide, calling it dephlogisticated air?
questions.explanation_correct: Priestley isolated oxygen but interpreted it within phlogiston theory. Lavoisier later named oxygen and explained its role in combustion; Scheele also isolated it independently.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The gas Priestley collected in the experiment was oxygen, not nitrogen, hydrogen or chlorine.

questions.question: What was the name of the early 20th-century hypothesis suggesting that Earth's landmasses were once a single supercontinent?
questions.explanation_correct: Alfred Wegener argued that continents had moved and had once been joined. Modern plate tectonics provides a broader explanation involving moving lithospheric plates.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Continental drift names Wegener’s early hypothesis; seafloor spreading and plate tectonics are later, related concepts.

questions.question: Which French astronomer calculated Neptune’s predicted position and sent it to Johann Galle before its 1846 observation?
questions.explanation_correct: Urbain Le Verrier sent the prediction that guided Galle’s search. John Couch Adams independently calculated a position for the suspected planet.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Adams also made an independent prediction, but Le Verrier sent the specific calculation used by Galle. Galle made the observation.

questions.question: What is the name of Saturn's largest moon, discovered by Christiaan Huygens?
questions.explanation_correct: Titan is the largest moon of Saturn and was discovered by Christiaan Huygens in 1655. It was the first moon of Saturn ever found.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Rhea, Iapetus and Enceladus are other Saturnian moons, discovered by astronomers other than Huygens.

questions.question: Who is credited with discovering the neutron?
questions.explanation_correct: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932 through experiments involving beryllium radiation. This discovery was crucial for modern nuclear physics.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other physicists made major contributions to atomic and nuclear theory, but they are not credited with discovering the neutron. Their work is related, not the specific breakthrough asked here.

questions.question: Who discovered the positron?
questions.explanation_correct: Carl Anderson discovered the positron in 1932 while studying cosmic rays. It was the first identified antiparticle.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other scientists were important in particle and atomic physics, but they are not credited with the positron’s discovery. Paul Dirac predicted it theoretically rather than observing it experimentally.

questions.question: Who is traditionally credited with the discovery of the cell from cork observations?
questions.explanation_correct: Robert Hooke examined thin slices of cork and coined the term “cell” in 1665. His observations marked an early milestone in microscopy and biology.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are associated with microscopy or cell theory, but not with the original cork observation and naming of cells. Antonie van Leeuwenhoek observed microorganisms instead.

questions.question: Which microscopist reported observations of living microscopic organisms, including bacteria, in the 1670s?
questions.explanation_correct: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek described microscopic organisms he called animalcules, including bacteria. Robert Hooke had earlier illustrated microscopic moulds.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Hooke contributed major early microscopy, but Leeuwenhoek reported the living microorganisms described here. Pasteur and Mendel worked later.

questions.question: Who identified the A, B and O human blood groups at the beginning of the twentieth century?
questions.explanation_correct: Karl Landsteiner’s blood-mixing experiments established the ABO group system and helped make transfusions safer.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other scientists contributed to medicine and biology but did not establish the ABO group classification.

questions.question: Who discovered phosphorus?
questions.explanation_correct: Hennig Brand discovered phosphorus in 1669 while experimenting with urine. He was the first person known to isolate the element.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other chemists were influential in the development of chemistry, but they are not credited with the discovery of phosphorus. Their work concerned other elements or chemical principles.

questions.question: Which explorer led the Spanish expedition that crossed the Isthmus of Panama and reached the Pacific in 1513?
questions.explanation_correct: Vasco Núñez de Balboa’s expedition reached the Pacific from the American side in 1513, guided and accompanied by Indigenous people.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Magellan later reached the Pacific from the Atlantic through the strait that bears his name; the other options are associated with different expeditions.

questions.question: Who brought Machu Picchu to international attention in 1911?
questions.explanation_correct: Hiram Bingham reached Machu Picchu in 1911 and helped bring it to international attention. Indigenous and local residents already knew the site and guided him.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other archaeologists worked on different projects; Bingham led the 1911 expedition described.

questions.question: Who is credited with discovering the Rosetta Stone?
questions.explanation_correct: Pierre-François Bouchard is credited with the stone's discovery in 1799 at Fort Julien in Egypt. His find became crucial for deciphering ancient Egyptian writing.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are notable figures in Egyptology or archaeology, but they did not discover the Rosetta Stone. They are associated with later interpretation or excavation work.

questions.question: Who discovered Java Man?
questions.explanation_correct: Eugène Dubois discovered Java Man in the 1890s in what is now Indonesia. He identified the fossils as an important early human ancestor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other scientists are famous paleoanthropologists, but they did not discover Java Man. Their work was on different fossil finds and sites.

questions.question: Who discovered jumping genes?
questions.explanation_correct: Barbara McClintock discovered transposable elements, often called jumping genes, in maize. Her work transformed genetics and earned her the Nobel Prize.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures are major names in genetics and molecular biology, but they did not identify transposable elements. Their discoveries were in different areas of heredity and DNA research.

questions.question: Which pair announced the discovery of radium in 1898 in work with Gustave Bémont?
questions.explanation_correct: Marie and Pierre Curie identified radium with the chemist Gustave Bémont in 1898. Isolation of pure radium compounds followed later.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other pairs did not announce radium’s discovery. Becquerel had earlier discovered radioactivity.

questions.question: Which Dutch scientist in 1898 interpreted the filterable tobacco mosaic agent as a new kind of infectious entity?
questions.explanation_correct: Martinus Beijerinck extended filtration experiments and described the agent as a contagious living fluid. Dmitri Ivanovsky had reported its filterability earlier in 1892.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Ivanovsky’s earlier contribution was important; the question asks for the Dutch scientist who interpreted the result in 1898.

questions.question: Which planet was discovered by William Herschel in 1781?
questions.explanation_correct: William Herschel discovered Uranus in 1781, expanding the known boundaries of the Solar System. It was the first planet found with a telescope in modern times.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are planets, but they were known long before Herschel's observation or discovered later by other astronomers. They are not the planet identified in 1781.

questions.question: The world's first widely used antibiotic was derived from which fungal genus?
questions.explanation_correct: The genus Penicillium is the source of the antibiotic penicillin, which revolutionized medicine.
questions.explanation_incorrect: While Aspergillus and Rhizopus are common molds, they were not the source of the first major antibiotic.

questions.question: Which particle did J. J. Thomson discover?
questions.explanation_correct: J. J. Thomson discovered the electron through cathode ray experiments in 1897. This was a major breakthrough in atomic physics.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are subatomic particles, but they were discovered by different scientists at different times. They do not match Thomson's discovery.

questions.question: Which physician published De Motu Cordis in 1628, describing blood circulation?
questions.explanation_correct: William Harvey described systemic blood circulation and the pumping action of the heart in De Motu Cordis.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Malpighi later observed capillaries. Earlier scholars also contributed to understanding circulation.

questions.question: Which pharaoh's tomb was found by Howard Carter in 1922?
questions.explanation_correct: Howard Carter found the nearly intact tomb of Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings in 1922. The discovery became one of the most famous archaeological finds in history.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are Egyptian rulers, but their tombs were not the one discovered by Howard Carter in 1922. They are from the same historical setting, but they are not the correct match.

questions.question: What shape was identified for DNA's structure?
questions.explanation_correct: DNA was shown to have a double helix structure. This description refers to two intertwined strands.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options describe different molecular forms or structures, not the canonical DNA arrangement.

questions.question: What phenomenon did Becquerel discover while studying uranium salts?
questions.explanation_correct: Becquerel discovered radioactivity from the spontaneous emissions of certain substances. His work helped launch the study of nuclear physics.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are different physical or chemical processes and were not Becquerel's discovery.

questions.question: Which ocean did Vasco Núñez de Balboa’s expedition reach after crossing the Isthmus of Panama in 1513?
questions.explanation_correct: Balboa’s expedition reached the Pacific from the American side. Indigenous peoples already knew the ocean.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The expedition reached the Pacific rather than the Atlantic, Indian or Arctic Ocean.

questions.question: Which ship is associated with Darwin's voyage that shaped his discoveries?
questions.explanation_correct: Charles Darwin sailed on HMS Beagle during the voyage that informed his ideas about evolution. The ship is closely linked to his scientific work.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other ships are famous historical vessels, but they are not the one associated with Darwin's voyage.

questions.question: Which ancient city was excavated by Heinrich Schliemann?
questions.explanation_correct: Heinrich Schliemann is known for excavations at Troy, which connected archaeology with Homeric legend. His work made the site famous worldwide.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other cities are important archaeological sites, but they were not the main excavation associated with Schliemann.

questions.question: At which Tanzanian gorge did members of the Leakey family discover important early hominin fossils?
questions.explanation_correct: Olduvai Gorge is a Tanzanian fossil site associated with discoveries by the Leakey family, including Mary Leakey’s OH 5.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Olduvai is part of the broader East African Rift region; the question asks for the specific gorge.

questions.question: Which disease was addressed by Banting's insulin research?
questions.explanation_correct: Banting's work helped develop insulin treatment for diabetes. This discovery transformed care for people with the disease.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are medical conditions, but they were not the disease treated by insulin therapy.

questions.question: Which element was isolated by Priestley and Scheele?
questions.explanation_correct: Joseph Priestley and Carl Wilhelm Scheele independently isolated oxygen. Their interpretations differed from Lavoisier’s later oxygen theory.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Hydrogen, nitrogen and chlorine are different elements from the gas independently isolated in these experiments.

questions.question: Which positively charged particle did Rutherford identify?
questions.explanation_correct: Rutherford is credited with identifying the proton as a positively charged particle in the atom. This was a key step in atomic theory.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other particles are distinct subatomic entities, but they were not the one Rutherford identified in this context.

questions.question: What type of agent did Beijerinck identify as a new infectious entity?
questions.explanation_correct: Beijerinck concluded that the infectious agent he studied was a virus. His work helped establish virology as a separate field.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different kinds of microorganisms, but they do not match Beijerinck's conclusion.

questions.question: Who is credited with discovering Pluto?
questions.explanation_correct: Clyde Tombaugh is the astronomer who discovered Pluto in 1930. His observation work at Lowell Observatory led to the planet's identification.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are astronomers associated with major work in astronomy, but they did not discover Pluto. They belong to the same field yet are not the correct discoverer.

questions.question: Which planet was NOT known to ancient astronomers?
questions.explanation_correct: Neptune was discovered in 1846 via mathematical prediction, whereas Mars, Venus, and Jupiter were known since ancient times.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mars, Venus, and Jupiter are visible to the naked eye and have been observed since antiquity.

questions.question: Who discovered the electron?
questions.explanation_correct: J. J. Thomson discovered the electron through cathode-ray experiments in 1897. His work established the existence of a smaller constituent of the atom.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other physicists made major atomic discoveries, but not this one. They are plausible distractors because they are all associated with subatomic physics.

questions.question: What particle was discovered by James Chadwick?
questions.explanation_correct: The neutron is the particle discovered by James Chadwick in 1932. It was identified as a neutral component of the atomic nucleus.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are subatomic particles, but they are not the one Chadwick discovered. They fit the same category while remaining incorrect.

questions.question: Which English chemist isolated oxygen by heating mercuric oxide in 1774?
questions.explanation_correct: Joseph Priestley collected oxygen in 1774. Carl Wilhelm Scheele also isolated it independently; Lavoisier later named it and explained its role in combustion.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Lavoisier contributed to identifying oxygen’s role, but Priestley performed the 1774 mercury oxide experiment described.

questions.question: Which element was first isolated by Hennig Brand?
questions.explanation_correct: Hennig Brand isolated phosphorus from urine around 1669. It is commonly described as the first element discovered in modern times.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sulfur, carbon and arsenic were known before Brand’s isolation of phosphorus.

questions.question: Who is credited with discovering the ABO blood group system?
questions.explanation_correct: Karl Landsteiner discovered the ABO blood group system in 1900 and 1901, for which he received the Nobel Prize.
questions.explanation_incorrect: While Jan Janský later classified blood groups, Landsteiner is the credited discoverer of the system itself.

questions.question: What term did later scientists use for Mendel’s discrete hereditary factors?
questions.explanation_correct: Mendel inferred that hereditary factors are passed from parents to offspring. The modern term gene was introduced later; his experiments distinguished alternative forms now called alleles.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Chromosomes carry many genes; alleles are alternative forms of a gene. The nucleus is a cellular structure.

questions.question: Which Inca site did Hiram Bingham visit in 1911 with guidance from local residents?
questions.explanation_correct: Machu Picchu was known locally before Bingham’s 1911 visit; his expedition helped bring it to wider international attention.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Tikal, Pompeii and Angkor Wat are other archaeological sites, not the Peruvian site visited by Bingham.

questions.question: Which ocean did Columbus cross on his 1492 voyage from Spain to the Caribbean?
questions.explanation_correct: The 1492 expedition crossed the Atlantic. The ocean had been crossed by Norse seafarers centuries earlier.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The 1492 route crossed the Atlantic, not the Indian, Pacific or Arctic Ocean.

questions.question: What common name was given to the Homo erectus fossils found at Trinil on the Solo River in 1891?
questions.explanation_correct: Java Man refers to Homo erectus fossils recovered by Eugène Dubois’s team at Trinil. The find was important evidence for human evolution.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Lucy is an Australopithecus fossil, Neanderthal refers to a different hominin, and Homo habilis is a different species.

questions.question: Which geneticist is best known for research on transposable elements, often called jumping genes?
questions.explanation_correct: Barbara McClintock pioneered work showing that genes can move within chromosomes, earning her recognition for transposable elements. Her maize experiments were foundational in genetics.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other scientists are known for DNA structure, inheritance laws, or molecular biology more broadly. They are not associated with jumping genes.

questions.question: Who discovered the atomic nucleus through the gold foil experiment?
questions.explanation_correct: Ernest Rutherford inferred the existence of a small, dense atomic nucleus from the gold foil experiment. This transformed the atomic model.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other physicists are associated with electron discovery, atomic theory, or quantum ideas. They did not discover the nucleus.

questions.question: Which physician worked with pathologist Robin Warren on Helicobacter pylori and its link to peptic ulcers?
questions.explanation_correct: Barry Marshall collaborated with Robin Warren; Warren had first noticed bacteria in gastric biopsies before their joint investigations.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Koch, Pasteur and Fleming made other major contributions to microbiology, but were not Warren’s collaborator on this work.

questions.question: Which ancient city was famously buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius?
questions.explanation_correct: Pompeii was buried by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE. Its preservation made it one of archaeology's most important sites.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other cities were major ancient centers, but they were not destroyed and preserved by Vesuvius. They have different historical contexts.

questions.question: Which astronomer discovered Pluto in 1930?
questions.explanation_correct: Clyde Tombaugh discovered Pluto while working at the Lowell Observatory. The discovery was announced in 1930.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other astronomers are linked to different discoveries or theories. They are not credited with finding Pluto.

questions.question: Which scientist famously identified the three main human blood groups (A, B, and O) in 1901?
questions.explanation_correct: Karl Landsteiner's work identified the ABO system, revolutionizing safe blood transfusions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures are prominent in hematology or medicine but did not discover the original ABO system.

questions.question: Which archaeologist is known for the systematic excavation methods used at Pompeii?
questions.explanation_correct: Giuseppe Fiorelli introduced systematic excavation techniques at Pompeii, including the famous plaster-cast method. His work greatly improved archaeological documentation.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other archaeologists are known for discoveries at different sites or regions. They did not introduce the Pompeii methods attributed to Fiorelli.

questions.question: Which American fossil hunter found early Tyrannosaurus rex remains in Montana in 1902?
questions.explanation_correct: Barnum Brown collected the 1902 Montana specimen later named Tyrannosaurus rex by Henry Fairfield Osborn.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Cope and Marsh discovered many western American dinosaurs, but the 1902 T. rex field discovery is associated with Brown.

questions.question: Which scientist is credited as a major contributor to determining DNA structure?
questions.explanation_correct: Rosalind Franklin’s X-ray diffraction work provided key evidence for the DNA double-helix model. Her data were central to understanding DNA structure.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other scientists are notable genetic researchers, but they are not the correct answer to the DNA-structure contribution asked here.

questions.question: Which Portuguese navigator led the first recorded European voyage around the Cape of Good Hope in 1488?
questions.explanation_correct: Bartolomeu Dias rounded southern Africa in 1488. Vasco da Gama later completed the sea voyage from Portugal to India.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Da Gama later sailed around the Cape to India; the others are associated with different expeditions. People in Africa knew these coasts before Europeans arrived.

questions.question: Who deciphered the meaning of ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs using the Rosetta Stone?
questions.explanation_correct: Jean-François Champollion established a decipherment of Egyptian hieroglyphs using several sources, including the Rosetta Stone and the Coptic language.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Thomas Young made important earlier contributions to interpreting the inscriptions, but Champollion is credited with establishing the wider decipherment.

questions.question: Barry Marshall and which other scientist were awarded the Nobel Prize for discovering Helicobacter pylori?
questions.explanation_correct: Barry Marshall and Robin Warren jointly discovered the bacterium's role in gastritis and peptic ulcers.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other scientists are famous microbiologists not associated with the discovery of H. pylori.

questions.question: Who isolated potassium and several other elements through early electrolysis experiments?
questions.explanation_correct: Humphry Davy used electrolysis to isolate reactive elements such as potassium and sodium. His experiments transformed early chemistry.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other chemists made major contributions to science, but they are not the figure associated with isolating these elements.

questions.question: Which pair were among the scientists on the 1977 expedition that discovered hydrothermal vent communities at the Galápagos Rift?
questions.explanation_correct: Jack Corliss and Robert Ballard were members of the team involved in the 1977 Galápagos Rift discovery; the finding was a collaborative expedition.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other pairs were not the scientists identified with the 1977 vent expedition.

questions.question: Who is credited with discovering the fossil known as Lucy?
questions.explanation_correct: Donald Johanson and his colleagues discovered the Lucy skeleton in Ethiopia in 1974; Tom Gray was with Johanson when it was found.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Leakey family made other major discoveries; the question concerns the team associated with Lucy.

questions.question: Which astronomer is credited with discovering Saturn's moon Titan?
questions.explanation_correct: Christiaan Huygens discovered Titan in 1655 using a telescope. It was the first known moon of Saturn found by a scientist.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other astronomers made major contributions to astronomy, but they are not the discoverer asked for here.

questions.question: Which virologist shared the 2008 Nobel Prize for HIV discovery with Françoise Barré-Sinoussi?
questions.explanation_correct: Luc Montagnier and Françoise Barré-Sinoussi shared the HIV-related portion of the 2008 Nobel Prize. Jean-Claude Chermann was also part of the research team.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Barré-Sinoussi is the scientist named in the question; Gallo also made important contributions to HIV research, while zur Hausen was awarded for HPV work.

questions.question: Who led the British expedition that reached the South Pole in 1912?
questions.explanation_correct: Robert Falcon Scott led the Terra Nova Expedition to the South Pole. His party arrived in 1912 after Amundsen’s earlier successful journey.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other explorers are famous polar figures, but they are not the British expedition leader referenced here.

questions.question: Which astronomer is credited with the discovery of the minor planet Hilda?
questions.explanation_correct: Johann Palisa was an Austrian astronomer known for discovering many asteroids, including the minor planet Hilda. He was one of the most prolific discoverers of small bodies in the solar system.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are also astronomers, but they are not the credited discoverer of Hilda. Their discoveries are associated with different celestial objects.

questions.question: Which French chemist is credited with the discovery of chromium?
questions.explanation_correct: Nicolas-Louis Vauquelin is credited with discovering the element chromium in 1797. His work also led to the identification of other chemical substances.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other scientists were important chemists, but they are not the discoverer of chromium. Their contributions lie in different areas of chemistry.

questions.question: Which physiologist is associated with introducing the term hormone in 1905 after work on secretin?
questions.explanation_correct: Ernest Starling introduced the term hormone; he and William Bayliss had discovered secretin together in 1902.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bayliss co-discovered secretin with Starling, but the question asks for the physiologist associated with introducing the term.

questions.question: Which fossil-bearing site in the Canadian Rockies is world-famous for its exceptional preservation of soft-bodied organisms from the Cambrian period?
questions.explanation_correct: The Burgess Shale is a fossil field in British Columbia known for its 508-million-year-old specimens.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Chengjiang is in China, Messel Pit is in Germany, and La Brea is a much younger Quaternary site.

questions.question: Which Dutch explorer for the East India Company was the first European to encounter Van Diemen's Land and the South Island of New Zealand?
questions.explanation_correct: Tasman reached these regions in 1642, though he initially named Tasmania after Anthony van Diemen.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Janszoon reached Australia earlier but not the islands mentioned; Magellan and Cook were not Dutch.

questions.question: Which particle was identified by Carl Anderson in 1932?
questions.explanation_correct: The positron was identified by Carl Anderson in 1932 as the electron's antiparticle. It was the first antimatter particle discovered.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are subatomic particles, but they were not the one discovered by Anderson in 1932. Their discovery histories are different.

questions.question: What is the common nickname of the Australopithecus afarensis fossil discovered in Ethiopia in 1974?
questions.explanation_correct: Lucy is the nickname of an Australopithecus afarensis skeleton found in Ethiopia in 1974. It is an early human relative; whether it was directly ancestral to modern humans is not established.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Ardi, Taung Child and Mrs. Ples refer to different hominin specimens.

questions.question: Which bacterium is associated with the ulcer-causing organism identified by Barry Marshall and Robin Warren?
questions.explanation_correct: Helicobacter pylori is the bacterium identified by Barry Marshall and Robin Warren as a major cause of peptic ulcers. Their discovery transformed understanding of gastric disease.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are bacteria, but they are not the organism linked to that discovery. They cause different infections and conditions.

questions.question: Which manuscript collection was found in caves near Qumran beginning in 1947?
questions.explanation_correct: The Dead Sea Scrolls are the manuscript collection discovered in caves near Qumran starting in 1947. They are among the most important ancient textual finds ever made.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are also manuscript collections or texts, but they were found in different places and contexts. They are not the Qumran cave discoveries.

questions.question: Which oceanographic site is famous for the first discovery of hydrothermal vents in 1977?
questions.explanation_correct: The first known deep-sea hydrothermal vent communities were discovered by a scientific team at the Galápagos Rift in 1977.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge and Mariana Trench are different features. The broader 1977 research expedition also studied the East Pacific Rise; the first observed vent community was at the Galápagos Rift.
